Subject: POC success criteria & KPI alignment for Atlas Payments

Hi Claire / team,

Thanks again for the call today — great alignment on the integration approach. As promised, below is a concise proposal for POC success criteria and KPIs so we have a concrete evaluation plan heading into the trial. Attached is a working spreadsheet (poc-success-kpis.xlsx) and a draft evaluation-plan.docx.

High-level goal: validate that Redwood can meet Atlas Payments' latency, throughput, cost, and quality targets in a production-like workload.

Proposed success criteria / KPIs (minimal pass thresholds):
- Latency: p95 generation latency <= 200 ms for 1k-token prompts (target per route).
- Throughput: sustain 50 requests/sec (concurrent inference sessions) with tail-latency SLOs met; scale tests to 200 rps for burst capacity validation.
- Cost: effective cost per 1k tokens (gen + context) < $0.70 (target); model/quantization profiles should show forecasted cost savings if applicable.
- Quality: automatic metrics + human acceptability: automated rouge/f1 benchmarks on seeded eval set >= baseline; human-blind eval accept rate >= 90% for correctness/clarity on 200 samples.
- Error rate / failures: end-to-end error rate < 1% during steady-state test.
- Security/compliance: no customer data persists beyond agreed retention; audit logs present for all inference calls during POC.

Evaluation plan (phases & timeline):
1) Sandbox validation (Week 1): small dataset + sample prompts to validate integration and baseline latency on Redwood hosted dev endpoint. Deliverable: sandbox report and tuned model variant.
2) Integration POC (Weeks 2-3): run 2-week integration into Atlas staging with recorded traffic pattern (sanitized), measure p95/p99, throughput, and cost. Deliverable: POC runbook and results spreadsheet.
3) Scale/Burst test (Week 4): targeted load tests to validate autoscaling and burst behavior; measure reliability under synthetic spikes.

Owners: Jordan (sales/POC lead), Michael Chen (Atlas eng lead), Laura Bennett (Redwood CS owner), Stephanie Nguyen (Redwood performance lead).

Next steps:
- Jordan to share the attachments and this summary (done).
- Claire to confirm any additional KPIs or minimum thresholds and provide a sample eval dataset or prompt set.
- Schedule kickoff for Week 1 sandbox run (propose Mon 2 March / Tue 3 March).

Thanks — happy to iterate.

Best,
Jordan Blake
Senior Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference

Attachments: poc-success-kpis.xlsx, evaluation-plan.docx

Jordan — thanks for the clear recap. This aligns closely with what we discussed. A couple of additions/clarifications from our side: 

- Throughput: for our peak checkout flows we need to validate 100 concurrent sessions with median latency < 150ms; can Redwood include an additional burst target at 100 concurrent sessions?
- Quality evaluation: we can provide a 300-sample prompt set (sanitized) and would like to include a small set of edge-case prompts that historically cause issues.
- Cost: please include a short forecast showing cost impact for 1M requests/month at the POC settings vs optimized settings.

We're good to kick off the sandbox week of Mar 1 — Tue 3 March morning PST works for Michael and me. Please send a calendar invite.

Also, can you confirm whether Redwood will sign the standard data processing addendum for telemetry collected during the POC?

Claire
Head of Product | Atlas Payments
